_comment: Minimum tests that must EXECUTE per project. The control for defect class DC-012: a crashed test host reports success with a smaller count, and nothing else notices. Raise these with `python tools/verify-test-run.py --update` when you add tests; never lower one to make a run pass. Keys with a suffix are HALVES of a project run on one OS; `splits` says which halves must account for which whole, and verify-test-run checks that sum on every invocation, on both operating systems. AiDe.Core.Tests.nonportable is [Trait("Platform","Windows")] only - kernel32, powershell.exe, the net10.0-windows daemon, and tests that assert Windows path semantics on purpose. There is no quarantine category: every test that merely failed on Linux was diagnosed and fixed (INV-0005).
_baselineBump: 2026-09-10, front-door F2 (the front door: sheet, File menu, session document, canvas modes) plus FX2 (two POSIX path-semantics defects). AiDe.App.Tests 400 -> 456 (F2's 56 surface, sheet, menu, canvas-mode, retain-oracle, permission-ordinal, run-log-reservation, lease and race tests); AiDe.Core.Tests 2037 -> 2041, portable 1885 -> 1889 (FX2's four path tests), nonportable unchanged at 152. MEASURED ON THE MERGED TREE, all four keys, not apportioned and not carried over from branch runs: --filter Platform!=Windows gave 1889, --filter Platform=Windows gave 152, the whole Core run gave 2041, and 1889 + 152 = 2041, so the split invariant holds by OBSERVATION rather than by arithmetic. App was run from the PowerShell console host (DC-117: it hangs under a console-less host and produces no result file at all). verify-test-run.py --update was NEVER run: it skips the split invariant (:193) and returns 0 unconditionally (:269), so it cannot be the thing that sets the gate. CHECK mode is the standing gate; this bump is a separate recorded act, counter-signed by the four runs quoted above. Every floor raised; none lowered.
